failure_case.summary: US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.
US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: signal_chile_flu has the strongest combined support (score=7) and the richest set of relationships to the failed prediction. In the support subgraph it is simultaneously a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the target (signal_us_hosp) and has both IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF edges into the mechanism (eq_us_flu_base). By contrast, the next-ranked candidate (signal_australia_flu, score=5) lacks an IMPORTATION_LINK to the mechanism (it is only a possible driver and a leading indicator), and the travel-pressure candidate (signal_travel_pressure, score=4) lacks an explicit LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR relationship to the target. The presence of both an importation linkage into the mechanism and an independent leading-indicator relationship to the hospitalization signal makes Chile influenza activity the most plausible hidden driver for an underpredicted/missed peak in US hospitalizations.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add an explicit mechanistic input from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base: create or activate a driver term that feeds Chile influenza activity into the US mechanism (edge: signal_chile_flu -> eq_us_flu_base) with a short-to-moderate lag parameter (test a small set of lags) so that the mechanism can be seeded/adjusted by observed Chile activity. This is a minimal change that leverages the existing IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF edges and the LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR relationship to the target.
llm_output.caveat: The graph evidence supports association and plausible importation timing but does not prove causality or the correct lag/weight. Implementing the edit requires testing lag/weight values and checking for confounding seasonal patterns (e.g., concurrent drivers) to avoid overfitting or false attribution.
